title: Make dashboard polling tests advance on controlled time and observed replies

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: Running Cursor sessions recovery after unreachable

**Outcome: Caught.**

## Selected promise

- Story: SEED-262#drive-polls-with-time-and-replies (`.planning/seeds/SEED-262-faster-dashboard-test-feedback.md`), revision a11f07fe1e209663dd92b5afb5e48e33cc2f7be8 (implementation 655412c63).
- Promise (third key example, "recovery" in the goal): after a controlled poll shows the unreachable state, the next poll's reply restores the working session ("The Cursor runner is running." with the `working` row). Chosen because the implementation's discrimination faults (early ask, overlap, ignored visibility, uncleared collapse, scheduled reveal, ignored unreachable) covered entering the unreachable state but not leaving it.
- Plausible fault: a latching error state. In `dashboard/src/RunningCursorSessions.tsx`, the read's `.then` (line 93) changed from `setListed(answer ?? "unanswered")` to a functional update that keeps the prior value when it was `runner: "unreachable"`, so polling continues but later answers never replace the unreachable display.

## Fixture and assertion

- Test: `dashboard/frontend-tests/cursor-runner-sessions-ui.spec.ts`, case "while expanded, the list says it is reading, then follows each later read: unreachable, restored, and running with no held sessions" (paused page clock, held route reads from `holdCursorSessionsReads`, MakeMe ad hoc Cursor launch record).
- Maintained assertion: line 207, `await expect(region).toContainText("The Cursor runner is running.")` right after `answerNextRead(heldSessions)` that follows the unreachable answer.
- Fixture and assertion were left intact; only the production line was changed.

## Runs

Scratch checkout: local clone at `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/2991d794/tmp/ic-scratch`, detached at a11f07fe, after `setup-native.mjs npm` and `browser`; pre-probe `git status --short` empty. Execution checkout untouched. Command (prefixed with `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES caffeinate -s -i`):
`./node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config dashboard/playwright.config.ts --reporter=list -g "follows each later read" 'frontend-tests/cursor-runner-sessions-ui\.spec\.ts$'`

1. Baseline: 1 passed (case 1.5 s, runner 4.7 s); the selected case ran.
2. Fault (restore armed with a shell trap): 1 failed (case 6.0 s). Failure at line 207: expected "The Cursor runner is running.", received "Running Cursor sessionsThe Cursor runner cannot be reached." after the 5 s expect timeout. Reach: `answerNextRead(heldSessions)` completed (the third read arrived on the advanced page clock and was answered), so the failure is at the intended assertion on the intended path, and the received text is the wrong behavior the fault produces (stale unreachable state instead of the restored session).
3. Restore: original file copied back; `git diff --quiet` clean and `git status --short` matches the empty pre-probe state. Same command: 1 passed (case 976 ms, runner 1.7 s).

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** Measured, Playwright list reporter: baseline 4.7 s runner (case 1.5 s); fault 6.0 s case (runner total not recorded separately; dominated by the 5 s expect timeout); restored 1.7 s runner (case 976 ms).
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no human took part in this check; no separate measure exists.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable: no separately supported token or tool-time measure was exposed to the agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 70381 ms (measured), from 1794121834138 to 1794121904519 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
